title: LLM Alignment--Utility Asymmetry under Semantic-Preserving Transformations
abstract: arXiv:2609.32717v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) alignment is intended to ensure that models remain helpful and safe, but its stability under input distributional shift is not yet fully understood. Prior work shows that aligned models can fail under jailbreak prompts, alternative encodings, and cross-lingual transfer, yet these failures are usually studied as attacks rather than controlled probes of alignment generalization. Moreover, existing evidence is largely grounded in natural language variation already represented during pretraining, leaving unresolved whether alignment generalizes with semantic content or remains tied to superficial surface patterns. In this paper, we study this question using synthetic semantic-preserving transformations that are rule-based and invertible, preserving task-relevant meaning while shifting inputs beyond standard linguistic variation. translated_title: 大语言模型对齐——语义保持变换下的效用不对称性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）对齐旨在确保模型保持有用和安全，但其在输入分布偏移下的稳定性尚未得到充分理解。先前的研究表明，经过对齐的模型在面对越狱提示词、替代编码以及跨语言迁移时可能失效，然而这些失效通常被当作攻击来研究，而非作为对齐泛化能力的受控探针。此外，现有证据主要建立在预训练中已经出现过的自然语言变化之上，因此对齐究竟是随语义内容而泛化，还是仍然依附于表层的表面模式，这一问题仍未得到解决。在本文中，我们使用基于规则且可逆的合成语义保持变换来研究这一问题，这些变换在保持任务相关语义的同时，将输入偏移至标准语言变化之外。在四个开源权重模型和四个商业模型上，分别在微调和……
tldr: 本文提出基于规则且可逆的语义保持变换作为受控探针，系统考察LLM对齐在分布偏移下的泛化能力，发现模型在语义保持不变的输入变换下呈现效用不对称性，表明对齐可能依附于表面模式而非随语义内容泛化。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces rule-based, invertible semantic-preserving transformations as controlled probes of LLM alignment, revealing a utility asymmetry across eight models under such meaning-preserving shifts, which suggests alignment may remain tied to superficial surface patterns rather than generalizing with semantic content.
